Yes. I’d add a one-shot command option:

```sh
mise bootstrap --adopt <url> --replace-history --yes
```

`--replace-history` would:

- Fetch and validate the remote as a mise setup repository.
- Acquire the history locks so the watcher cannot recreate a checkpoint mid-operation.
- Discard the unrelated local branch using an atomic ref update.
- Preserve its previous commit in the reflog for short-term recovery.
- Reuse the normal fresh-adoption and conflict checks.

I would not make this a persistent setting: a watcher must never automatically discard divergent local history. I also prefer `--replace-history` over `--force-history` because it states exactly what will be destroyed.

This is a meaningful destructive-behavior addition, so I want your call: should I implement `--replace-history` as a separate PR?
